review_candidates.title: QA Specialist (EN>KR)
review_candidates.description: Job QA Specialist (EN>KR) Description Position Title QA specialist for English to Korean Position Overview This role is responsible for subtitle, template and transcription QA responsibilities to ensure high-quality localization. The QA Specialist will review, edit and proofread subtitles, template, transcription and any reference documents for linguistic accuracy, and ensure all client guidelines, requirements, and feedback are understood and incorporated into deliverables, maintaining creative integrity and client specifications. About The Team (Localization) Localization is the process of translating and adapting content to specific geographical regions for consumption in local markets. Though many services make up the elements of the localization process including subtitling and dubbing, the goal of localization is to be authentic to the content being created, protecting the creative vision, specifically for a target market, no matter their language, culture, or location. Deluxe is one of the world’s leading localization providers to the entertainment industry. We provide clients and therefore end users with a worldwide service offering in over 50 languages for theatrical, home entertainment, broadcast TV and streaming services. Main Duties A Day in the Life of this position would include the following : Conduct subtitle, template and transcription reviews, ensuring grammar, spelling, punctuation, consistency, and fluency. Escalate quality issues and collaborate with production teams for timely resolution. Validate feedback with language leads and evaluators as needed. Adjust to the appropriate format, ensure the original content and accuracy for spoken dialogue and text elements. For template, annotate cultural and contextual notes to support other target languages’ localization. Ensure files are error free and finalize deliverables to meet the highest industry standards as well as unique client specifications. Train and onboard new QA Specialists, ensuring alignment with quality standards. Participate in internal training sessions to stay updated on industry standards and workflows. What You Bring Extensive experience in editing for subtitling and scripting. Strong Korean and English language skills, written and oral. Organized, detail-oriented, and capable of working under tight deadlines. Ability to handle multiple tasks while maintaining a high attention to detail. Strong collaboration skills and ability to work independently. Familiarity with Microsoft Office, Google Suite, and general software tools. Well-rounded knowledge of historical and contemporary events, cultural references, slang, and idioms. About The Company Deluxe, a subsidiary of Platinum Equity, is a global leader in media and entertainment services for film, video and online content. Since 1915, Deluxe has been the trusted partner for the world’s most successful Hollywood studios, independent film companies, TV networks, exhibitors, advertisers and others, offering best-in-class solutions in post-production, distribution, asset and workflow management, and cloud-based technologies. With headquarters in Los Angeles and offices around the globe, the company employs over 3,500 of the most talented individuals, developers, and industry veterans worldwide. For more information, please visit www.bydeluxe.com. Diversity Statement Deluxe is committed to inclusivity, fostering an environment where every employee feels comfortable bringing their full selves to work. It is our policy to provide equal employment opportunities to all applicants and employees. Applicants will receive consideration for employment without regard to, and will not be discriminated against, on the basis of race, color, religion, creed, national origin or ancestry, sex, age, physical or mental disability, veteran status, sexual orientation, gender identity or expression, genetic information or any other legally recognized protected basis under federal, state or local laws, regulations or ordinances. Deluxe will consider qualified applicants with criminal histories in a manner consistent with the requirements of applicable local, state and federal law. Applicants with disabilities may be entitled to reasonable accommodation under the terms of the Disabilities Act and certain state or local laws. A reasonable accommodation is a change in the way things are normally done which will ensure an equal employment opportunity without imposing undue hardship on Deluxe. Please inform the company's HR representative if you need assistance completing any forms or to otherwise participate in the application process.

review_candidates.title: Project Delivery & Strategy Partner
review_candidates.description: Location: Fully remote, anywhere in Canada Type: Full-time, Permanent Hours: Flexible. Our clients are in every province and territory, so some give-and-take on time zones comes with the job. Start here We don't need someone to make decks that sit in a folder. We need someone who can design a plan and actually get the thing built. The kind of person who turns "we've been talking about this for ten years" into "we broke ground in the spring." Once a Nation's funding is approved, you own it. You run the project to completion, keep Eve, our delivery platform, current, and keep the Nation informed. Some days you'll be on a call with Chief and Council. Every day, you're the reason the work in front of them is solid and on schedule. This is an early role on a small team, so there's real room to grow into leading one. About us melyn helps First Nations across Canada plan, fund, and build. Housing, infrastructure, governance, economic development, the grants that pay for all of it, and the software that ties it together. We build long plans, win real funding, and stick around to deliver. When the work goes well, a community gets housing, a Nation owns a business, and a Council leads with confidence. What you'd actually do Run your own client engagements end to end in alignment with grant proposals: scope it, plan it, deliver it on time without anyone chasing you Be the person your clients talk to: build the relationship, run the calls, and keep Chief, Council, and staff moving Lead the thinking and writing on the big pieces: community plans, economic development plans, feasibility studies, business cases, and governance reviews Proactively communicate internally with leadership and team mates to ensure the project keeps moving and stays on schedule Build budgets and financial models that hold up in front of Council, a funder, and an auditor Know what your funder expects: milestones, reporting, claims, and close out, and deliver on them What we're looking for Three or so years in strategy, consulting, economic development, project management, or advisory work. Have less, but real drive and a track record of getting things done? We'd still like to hear from you. A history of delivering hard things on time, running clients directly, and keeping several projects moving at once Strong writing and comfort with numbers. You can take a complex project and write five pages a Council or funder can act on, with a budget that survives scrutiny. Steady in a room with senior people, and you don't wait around to be told what to do Real respect for Indigenous self-determination, governance, and OCAP principles, and the humility to keep learning Bonus points Past work with or for First Nations, Métis, or Inuit communities, organizations, or governments CPA, CFA, PMP; interested in pursuing any of those; or a strong head for numbers or project management A background in economic development, infrastructure, real estate, energy, forestry, or natural resources Comfort with AI tools (Claude) or building processes that help you work faster Who you are You own every project end to end. Outreach goes out without anyone prompting you, updates land every week, and nothing sits waiting on you. When a Nation asks for something, it's back to them within a couple of days or they know why. This is a fast paced, high output team. You solve availability gaps rather than explain them, because slow turnaround on Nation work costs trust. You want to look back in a few years and point at real things that exist because you made them happen. What you get Pay starts at $60,000 and rises with experience, plus an annual bonus tied to company success and your own performance Health, dental and life coverage, flexible time off, and a vacation entitlement that grows with your tenure Credit for what you ship, not how long you've been at it A team of experts to learn from and lean on, and a genuine path to leading as we grow Fully remote, work from anywhere in Canada A real platform behind you: melynBrain, our grant tools, an analyst bench, and document pipelines that take the grunt work off your plate

review_candidates.description: About Endeavor Endeavor is the leading network of entrepreneurs scaling exceptional businesses around the world. Founded in 1997, we exist to develop thriving entrepreneurial ecosystems in places where talent is abundant, but capital and opportunity are not. Our Model Select: We identify entrepreneurs with the greatest potential and introduce them to Endeavor through a rigorous, value-add selection journey. Advance: To advance the field of global entrepreneurship, Endeavor publishes data-driven research and thought leadership based on our 30 years of experience in Elsewhere markets. Endeavor supports 3,000+ entrepreneurs across 50+ countries, including the founders of Replit, Mercado Libre, Careem, Rappi, Checkout.com, and ElevenLabs. About The Role Endeavor is building an original podcast. Each season runs six to eight episodes, and each episode is a deep dive into a single Endeavor market: how an entrepreneurial ecosystem came to exist, who built it, what it cost them, and why it happened there. Long-form, obsessively researched, structured as a narrative, and unembarrassed about being entertaining. The tone is pop history: funny where the story is funny, serious where it earns it, and full of detail a listener cannot find anywhere else. The Researcher will spend weeks focusing on one market at a time, centering each season's episodes on a city and the entrepreneurs who helped build its ecosystem, tracing how the city’s history and culture interconnect with the personal stories of the entrepreneurs and the network that grew around them. You will uncover the people, institutions, policies, places, and turning points that shaped the city’s trajectory. Then you will help turn it into something people want to listen to for ninety minutes. This is not a desk-research role and it is not a literature review. The work rewards someone who will pick up the phone, get on a plane, sit in an archive, and keep pulling on a thread after three people have told them it goes nowhere. Key Responsibilities Primary Research and Reporting (40%) : Own the reporting behind each episode from a blank page: build the source list, find the people who were in the room, and keep going until the story holds up from every angle Conduct interviews with entrepreneurs, co-founders, early employees, investors, regulators, competitors, journalists, and the people nobody thought to ask Travel to markets to report on the ground: visit the original office, walk the neighborhood, meet sources in person, and find the records that were never digitized Work across local-language press, corporate and court filings, trade publications, university and government archives, out-of-print books, and private collections Partner with Local Offices and the Endeavor network to open doors, then go well past the introductions they give you Verify the origin stories everyone repeats, including the ones Endeavor repeats, and establish what actually happened Story Development and Writing (30%) Turn several months of reporting into a narrative with a spine: characters, stakes, reversals, and a reason to still be listening at minute seventy Write episode outlines, narration drafts, host prep documents, and interview guides Find the connections that make an episode worth making: the detail in one founder's story that explains something structural about the whole market Accuracy and Source Integrity (15%) Maintain a documented source trail for every factual claim in every episode Fact-check to a standard that holds up to scrutiny from subjects, their lawyers, experts, and a local journalist all listening closely Flag where the record is thin, contested, or self-serving, and write around it honestly rather than smoothing it over Handle sensitive commercial, personal, and political material with judgment, including clear agreements about what is on the record Season Planning and Production (15%) Help select markets and central characters for each episode Maintain a story bank so the next episode never starts cold Work alongside producers, editors, and hosts through recording and post, including reviewing cuts for accuracy and narrative logic Feed research into companion material: show notes, written pieces, social content, and Endeavor's broader research and thought leadership Who You Are Strong commitment to Endeavor's mission 3-6 years in narrative or investigative research: late-night or satirical news, documentary, narrative podcast, long-form journalism, or book research A portfolio where the research is visible in the work. We will want to hear about something you found that nobody else had Excellent writer, with the ability to make a paragraph accurate and funny at the same time Independent-minded: comfortable questioning assumptions - including our own. Demonstrated ability to carry one story for weeks or months without losing momentum, interest, or rigor Comfortable cold-calling strangers, asking uncomfortable questions, and being told no repeatedly Strong interviewer: gets people comfortable enough to move beyond the talking points and into the real story Genuine curiosity: interested in the story before knowing anything about the topic Working proficiency in a second language is strongly preferred, particularly Spanish, Portuguese, Arabic, or Turkish. Comfortable working across cultures and time zones, and willing to travel internationally, sometimes on short notice. Discreet, with sound judgment on sensitive information about entrepreneurs, partners, and markets No prior experience in venture capital, startups, or emerging markets is required. Curiosity about them is. Position Details Position: Senior Manager, dual reporting into Chief of Staff and Head of Endeavor Insight Start date: November 2026 Location: Hybrid role based in Endeavor's NYC office, 3 days in office, 2 days flexible Compensation: $110k - $130k USD Schedule: full-time, 40 hours/week
